messages.content: The first general-purpose electronic computer, ENIAC (Electronic Numerical Integrator and Computer), was built in 1946 and weighed over 27 tons. It occupied a room-sized space and was used for calculating artillery trajectories during World War II. Interestingly, it was programmed using switches and cables, not software, and could perform 5,000 additions per second—remarkably fast for its time!
